name: pixel-flow-field
title: Pixel Flow Field
description: A dark canvas tiled with thousands of small square cells that drift along a noise flow, gather into a heavy word, and get shoved aside in a fading wake wherever the pointer moves.
use: A hero or section title should feel computational and react to the pointer while staying readable at rest.
avoid: It samples one short word: longer text shrinks until letters stop reading, and the loop runs whenever it is on screen.
a11y: The canvas is hidden from assistive tech and there is nothing to operate; reduced motion freezes one resolved frame. (keyboard: n-a, labels: n-a, reduced motion: respected)
looks: A near-black stage covered in a faint grid of tiny squares. Settled, the squares clump into a thick sans word, FLOW, drawn from visible dots, with a dim speckle of cells spread over the rest of the surface.
behaves: On arrival the dots float loose and scattered; within a couple of seconds they ease into the letterforms. Moving the pointer pushes nearby cells outward along the drag, leaving a temporary gap in the word that fills back in afterwards.
customise: Set the word with text, or point src at a CORS-readable image; cellSize, gap, shape, speed, pointer radius and strength, colors and scatter are props.
weight: heavy: Every visible frame draws up to 14,000 cells on a 2D canvas.
